tiers.specialist: A term whose meaning is set by a specific method, tool or paper. Forbidden in the opening paragraph. Must be defined within 200 characters of first use everywhere else.
tiers.domain: A term from chemistry, structural biology or machine learning that is unfamiliar to a non-specialist and takes one clause to define. Allowed anywhere after the opening paragraph, defined at first use.
tiers.general: A term whose plain-English meaning is close enough to its technical meaning that a non-specialist reads it correctly. Allowed in the opening paragraph.

terms.definition: A model that produces new examples of something rather than labelling examples it is given.
One example produced by a generative model, or one example drawn from a distribution.
Random values with no structure, used here as the starting point a generator refines away from.
How many times a generator is allowed to refine its answer before it has to hand it over.
Any measurement that can tell you the generator's output is wrong.
Checking a generated result against something that did not produce it.
A specific arrangement of atoms joined by bonds.
A large biological molecule; here, the target a designed molecule is meant to act on.
The protein a drug is intended to act on.
Having the size, greasiness and hydrogen-bonding profile typical of molecules that work as oral drugs.
Running a notebook against results committed to the bundle instead of recomputing them, so it works with no GPU and no download.
A generator trained to reverse a process that gradually turns data into noise, producing samples by taking many small denoising steps.
A generator trained to predict a velocity that carries a noise sample along a chosen path to a data sample, so sampling is following a current rather than reversing a random walk.
The network inside a diffusion model, which is given a noisy sample and its noise level and predicts the noise that was added.
A single number measuring how far one cloud of points sits from another, zero when the two are indistinguishable.
The small molecule that binds to a protein.
The cavity on a protein's surface where a ligand sits.
A molecule that sticks to its target strongly enough to matter.
The specific position and orientation of a ligand inside a pocket.
Predicting where and how a given molecule sits in a given pocket.
An experimentally measured structure of a protein with a ligand bound, the closest thing to ground truth in this material.
A tenth of a nanometre; a carbon-carbon bond is about 1.5 of them, so a 4 angstrom disagreement is a few bond lengths.
How many bonds an atom is allowed to have; breaking it makes a molecule impossible rather than merely unusual.
The chain of atoms running through a protein, without the side chains that decorate it.
Given a protein shape, predicting an amino-acid sequence that would fold into it.
Predicting the structure of a protein and a ligand together, as one complex, rather than separately.
Denoising diffusion probabilistic model, the formulation in which the network predicts the noise added at a given level and sampling walks that ladder back down.
A deterministic sampler for an already-trained diffusion network, used here as the control that separates path curvature from sampling noise.
The dial on the DDIM sampler that sets how much fresh noise is injected per step; at 1 it reproduces ancestral sampling, at 0 it is fully deterministic.
The original diffusion sampler, which adds a small amount of fresh noise back at every reverse step.
A choice of how fast signal fades to noise across the forward process, fading gently rather than crashing to zero early.
A function giving, for any position and time, which direction to move and how fast; what a flow-matching network learns.
The training objective that regresses on the velocity of one noise-to-data line at a time, which recovers the correct average field without ever writing it down.
The simplest ODE integrator: assume the velocity is constant across a step and move along it.
The property that rotating or translating a molecule rotates or translates the model's prediction the same way, so the model never relearns that physics is orientation-independent.
The mechanism a multi-modal flow model uses for categorical parts of a molecule, where labels jump between categories at learned rates instead of sliding continuously.
Running a continuous flow on coordinates and a categorical jump process on atom and bond types on one shared clock, so geometry and identity finish together.
Quantitative estimate of drug-likeness, one number from 0 to 1 rolling size, greasiness and hydrogen bonding together, where higher is more drug-like.
An estimate from 1 to 10 of how hard a molecule would be to make, where lower is easier.
A battery of pass/fail geometric checks on a pose, covering bond lengths, bond angles, internal clashes, ring flatness and distances to the protein and its cofactors.
A tool that reports strain energy and a protein-ligand interaction profile for a pose, quantities with no pass/fail line.
How far a pose's shape has been bent from the shape the molecule would relax into, in kcal/mol; here computed as the pose energy minus the energy of a relaxed conformer ensemble.
A 0-to-1 overlap score between two molecular fingerprints; meaningless without naming the fingerprint that produced it.
A bit vector summarizing a molecule's substructures; different fingerprint definitions give different, equally correct similarity numbers.
Generating a ligand while a protein pocket is held fixed and fed to the network as context at every step.
Fixing part of a molecule and letting the model generate the rest around it, borrowed from image models that fill a masked region.
A substructure a chemist wants to keep, typically because it is known to bind, is patent-free, or is easy to make.
The 0.5 threshold on Boltz-2's binary head, above which a molecule is called a binder; the continuous affinity value is not calibrated below it.
A confidence score for a predicted interface between two chains; high ipTM means the model is sure where the ligand sits, not that it belongs there.
A per-atom or per-residue confidence score from a structure predictor; Boltz-2 reports it on a 0-to-1 scale where ESMFold uses 0 to 100.

The distance between a designed protein backbone and the structure an independent predictor produces from the designed sequence alone; below 2 angstroms with pLDDT above 70 is the field's designability bar.
Whether a real sequence could encode a generated backbone, judged by the self-consistency test rather than by the generator's own confidence.
Named positions on a target's surface that a conditional backbone generator is told to aim its new binder at.
Rule-based structural alerts flagging substructures a screening library would normally exclude.
